ratings_why.fun: Every tier has a clear job and the board grows from 1/1 Sprouts to Register-fed capstones, with a real choice between the shop Wake and the fight Procession.
ratings_why.distinct: Folding sales into deaths is fresh, but slot-refilling death summons still play much like a Deathrattle tribe.

verdict_why: Old Fingers needs one rules fix: which stats a dead unit 'had then', and whether his own copies count as the next units to dig up.

points.text: Old Fingers copies units 'with the stats they had then', but a unit that died had 0 Health then. Say it means its stats before the fight's damage, or its full stats at death.

His copies are non-Sprout units that die, so they become the next 'last 2 laid to rest'. Say whether copies count; if they do, in-fight buffs like Undertaker's Attack or Raindrop's burst get kept and grow fight after fight.

The Procession build grows almost nothing permanently: Sprouts vanish after the fight and its buffs are auras. One fight-side card that banks a little from the fight's dead (as Ludwig does from the shop) would give that build a growth curve too.
Sexton's shop units 'have' the buff; say they keep it once bought, or the card reads as worthless.
Hired Mute grows Attack only, so its 3 Health folds by turn 5. +1/+1 once a turn might carry a seed further than +1 Attack twice.

standouts.why: Clerk Inkcap is a buffer that is also a fuse: Health buffs become fuel, and his death is one more mourner.
Bellows Puffwell turns selling into the build; it is the clearest Tier 5 direction card in the tribe.
Candlesnuff Abbess makes the front row a fountain of growing Sprouts, capped at six, which is a capstone worth building to.

weakest.why: Funeral Steward is one gold a turn on a vanilla body; it does its job but nobody will remember it.
Black-Gloved Undertaker kills a friend for a 1/1 Sprout and some Attack; it pays off only with an Ooze or a big Fruit unit on its left.
Hired Mute's Attack-only growth leaves a fragile seed.

flags.note: If his copies count as the last units laid to rest, in-fight buffs ratchet into the next fight's copies with no limit.
With Cordwainer each of six Sprout deaths makes two growing Sprouts, and Grandmother Bootlace adds the Register to each; capped, but very hot.
'The stats they had then' for a dead unit is not defined.
Not said whether a bought unit keeps Sexton's shop buff.
